item.title: Google Account Recovery for My Mother
item.dc:creator: mmichaelis0812
item.content:encoded:
You can't remember your Google Account. Not the email, or the password. It stinks getting old, not just the loss of memory, but retirement life is so dang complicated! Sigh, I am totally starting to feel this.

Let's break this problem down into smaller pieces to make it easier. The first problem, the most confounding of all, is the account email address. Without this we are stuck, so ignore the password problem at the moment (which later becomes very easy to solve anyway, so no worries 😁).

The account email address is very easily solved as long as you have another device already using this account. More than likely you do have a device using this account, probably whatever device you are using to read this blog. I know that my mother's computer is using her Google account and that her old phone is also still using this account, so it's not really even lost, just forgotten.

It's actually quite easy to remember this email address, as it is the one that you use for Gmail. I'm mentioning this to possibly spur your memory. If you seldom use that email account, continue, this is really quite easy.

You should be reading this blog post from a device which has your Google account, to make this very easy. If that's your computer, great, if that's a phone, be sure it's your phone that has the old account. I strongly recommend doing this from a computer as it will be easier to navigate the browser tabs, than from a phone. I'll proceed with instructions from a computer browser, however any browser on any device with your google account active will work.

The following image shows the default google page and in the upper right you will see your normal avatar for your google account, in my case, my beautiful profile pic. If you do not see this in the upper right of google, then switch to a different browser, if installed on your computer, or move to another device 😔. However, if you do see the following, simply clicking my gorgeous face, opens what you see below, along with my Google account email, as you can see below. This email shown is my google account email address.

Now click the following link Google, and it will open a new browser tab at google, then find your avatar in the upper right. Click your avatar to get your account email address! Easy as pie, which you now owe me!

Now for the easy, but frustrating password part. I say it's easy, because it will follow some logical steps, but hard for two reasons, one I still have to figure it out, and also because there may be a few steps. But still, it's no big deal, probably easier even than making that pie, but a lot less delicious 😏. Let me figure this out.................

10 seconds later.....Ok, we got this! Three clicks and I found myself able to change my password! Lets see if you can even warm a store bought pie in three clicks! 😁

Looking at the above image, you should see the words "Manage your Google Account", if not put your glasses on! 😂. Step one, click that button and Manage your Google Account! Exciting!

You will see something very similar to the following:

Two things of note are here. The first is the "Don't get locked out of your Google Account.", which I'll comment on in the following blog post (skip it for now) User Account Security when in Heaven

The second button is on the left menu, and it reads "Security". Please click it, and scroll down slightly, to reveal the following section of the page image "How you sign in to Google"

Yeah, even I don't want to spend the time to go through all of that, and fortunately we don't need to! See the word "Password", I'm thinking we should just click that and see what happens, but not yet!. I believe one of two things may happen, you will be asked for your google password (due to technical reasons I'll not explain), or you are home free!

If you see the following you must authenticate your Google account, probably with your forgotten password 😔. However, your current browser, more than likely will offer up that password for you to log in. The absolute majority of cases this will happen and you just click the button to continue. In my case I see the following, asking instead for my fingerprint to unlock access to my stored password. If you don't see the following, just move on to the next image.

Once you are here, you are home free! Here we can change your password quite easily:

Now you have a new and known password! Write it down, don't put it into a text file on your computer, those are so easily lost, as well as creating a security risk. There are password management vaults available, which I may blog on in the future. The immediate point here is to learn from having experienced memory loss or temporary confusion from the stress of these dang computers, and to secure your password so you don't have to follow these steps in the future.

I would suggest creating a new written list and attach it to something you will not lose, such as could be accomplished with a paperclip and a birth certificate, like your own. I'm not telling you what to do, I'm telling myself what to do.

I really hope my tone in conveying this was not condescending or belittling, which I'm aware I carry. I also hope this works for you and does not cause more confusion, as it's very possible these steps may not work, as it's impossible for me to actually know the state of security on your electronic devices, but I tried.

With Love,
Mikki ❤️

item.title: User Account Security when in Heaven
item.dc:creator: mmichaelis0812
item.content:encoded: SIDE NOTE (skip and come back here later!). You should come back here after we are done and click the "Add recovery email" button and add a trusted loved one's email address to your account, for the stated purpose of 'recovery,' as well as to put your Google account into a survivor's hands for when you leave this world, if you so desire. That person will have access to all your email, photos, documents, etc. within your Google account. If you go this path, it is critical that you also give this person your Google Account email address, which we previously extracted, having followed the steps above. If the person does not know your account email, they can not recover that account using the added recovery email. More than likely the person, or somebody else will know your Google gmail email account, but if not, your survivors will lose everything your Google Account is associated with, like FB, or possibly financial accounts. I think I'll write a post later about this process of organizing your account information, and how to properly add that information to legal will.

item.title: Unconditional Love
item.dc:creator: mmichaelis0812
item.content:encoded:
I discovered something new today. Unconditional Love. It is a spiritual principle that I've always thought I understood, and I did, it's obvious. It's the love I have for my children and grandchildren.

So today I was experiencing a situation with a friend and I felt the relationship was deteriorating, I made a big effort and I got stood up. I very gently lashed out and blocked her. I was pretty upset about it. I was really upset about it, nothing pretty about it.

So early that evening I reached out to this person to fix this terrible situation. They showed very little reaction to the whole thing.

OMG Mikki, are you that predictable that your friends know when ur just acting out dramatically and simply don't react? No. I think my friend is just really good at masking their pain. She cared.

Anyway, there was a minor dispute in chat about who contacted who more often, and who had invited the other to attend other meetings together. I ended this discussion in chat as that would have ended poorly I think. 50/50 chance we are both right once, yikes. I'm glad I preserved our friendship and we walked away.

The following are chat messages that I sent.

So, I’m going to sort of change the subject and tell you about some amazing technology I discovered. I know you like it when I tell you about this stuff. So I’ve been using AI quite a bit lately and I love it. I’m searching for a way to make money with it. Here is one idea.

It is possible for me to export a What’sApp chat, the entire chat, like every word Mauri and I have said to each other every. I can then very easily feed this data into my AI. It will read everything we have ever said.

I can then ask it questions about our discussion. For example

“Over the past month, who has reached out to who more often?”
“Who has asked the other to attend meetings other than Misfits?”
“Who is nicer?”
“Who shows more love and affection?”
“Please provide me a bullet point list of all topics we have ever discussed”
“How can I improve my communication with _”

The things you can ask it are limited only by your imagination.

I have actually already done this with my What’sApp chat with my friend Kris. She told me one night she thinks I’m not and I reciprocated. She said how happy that made her! Maybe I read it totally wrong and she was just happy that I found her hot, like I’d given her a compliment. I took it that we had just shown a mutual interest in each other. It kind of fizzled out, anyway at one point I asked my AI if Kris had feelings for me and AI told me yes. So, wtf, I guess my point is that AI was wrong 😥

Jesus, my life is so sad.

So I’m going to go do this now and see if what Mauri said was right. I hope she is right, otherwise, I don’t know what to think. Maybe I shouldn’t do this because I think Mauri is wrong.

Ok, I just had a much better idea! I’m just going to give Mauri a total free pass and just love her ❤️. I’m not going to worry about who’s right and all that, it doesn’t matter. All that matters is that I love Mauri and I know she loves me. ❤️

So it would seem that I’ve discovered I have unconditional love for Mauri and you! ❤️❤️ Wow, that really makes things a LOT easier now! 🌹💋

End of my chat

So

item.title: Multitasking, Humans, and Analogue Data
item.dc:creator: mmichaelis0812
item.content:encoded:
12/12/2024
TL;DR Lazy opinionated wandering thoughts.

I'm watching Ken Burn's "Leonardo da Vinci" and had a beautiful idea I wanted to write out and try to better understand, but damn it, a txt came in and I replied to it, and now I can't remember my idea. Sigh.

Humans multitask terribly in general, I believe. I wonder even if it's possible for our minds to encode and remember inspiration when it hits. I doubt it, I might remember it, and I might remember my subsequent thoughts it caused, but the inspiration itself is gone in a flash. We all know, it's a flash, not usually a thought, although sometimes rationalization spurs inspiration. It is very frustrating when I lose that moment.

I am the absolute worst at multitasking, which is why I very early learned multithreading aspects of software development. Interestingly enough, it was multitasking of the CPU, that created this new concept that humans should also be able to multitask.

When coding by hand 386 ASM when I was young, I learned something most do not know. CPU's multitask terribly. It's like a sprinter running in mud. It is absolutely the slowest operation of a CPU to switch context to another thread, and always will be. In other words, although a CPU can multitask with incredible accuracy, the speed at which multitasking occurs is terribly slow and a tremendous waste of computing power, not to mention electricity, which probably comes from fossil fuels.

A CPU with one thread running at 100mhz screams along at 100mhz. A CPU with two threads is not able to devote 50mhz to one thread and 50mhz to the other, because in the process of switching threads the CPU consumes an enormous amount of clock cycles. So the CPU overhead limits the frequency which can be shared by the threads. It gets much worse because the overhead exponentially grows depending on how often the CPU switches threads, to create the illusion both processes are running simultaneously and smoothly. The greater the frequency of thread switching, the less frequency is available to each process. Add in to this, the CPU having tens or hundreds of threads executing and the issue quickly becomes a deadlocked CPU, spending all its time switching threads, thereby unable to allocate any time for the threads to execute themselves. CPU multitasking, we very soon realized, is a process of exponentially diminishing returns. Yes, I'm well aware CPU's now have multicores, so the individual cores switch context less frequently. That's the whole purpose of multicores, better multitasking, as perceived by users, but still performed at great expense.

So why the world suddenly thought humans should have the ability to multitask is beyond me. Considering the soon learned failure of the CPU to multitask well at scale, was never conveyed to the public, we have continued for 30+ years thinking we should be able to accomplish this task, if we just tried hard enough. What a dumb thing for society to believe, as most humans obviously multitask terribly.

We as humans use technology to help us multitask better, with reminders and schedules. But really, is the human mind well suited to completely switch context, and put in equal effort to all tasks in their process? I would argue we are terrible at this and I never do it in my professional work, but let's see where this goes.

My reasoning is as such, although we perceive our conscious thought as the producers of our minds, it is but a component, essentially just the typewriter, the part of our mind that puts our thoughts into words that we then convey. But where do these words come from, more specifically, where does the inspiration for this output come from? Essentially, my question is this, how does multitasking effect the mind's process of creation?

I have no idea, I could actually argue either side of that question, but my gut tells me that long periods of thought on a single subject, with occasional breaks works best for me. It was smoking that made me realize this to be true in my life. I would work on a problem at my desk for an hour, then go out to smoke, and a solution would very frequently pop into my mind from nowhere. Obviously during the smoke break, I'd still be pondering the question, and receiving input and conversation from colleagues, which was when the spark of inspiration frequently took place. I was lucky back then, as currently I perform all my work totally isolated. Sigh.

I realize my view here is very limited regarding multitasking, and that there are many people very good at this skill, and there are many professions where it is required to be performed well, such as parenting, the absolute basis of human existence.

Possibly even, my view is totally wrong because a primitive human hunter stalking prey, would have to be multitasking an enormous amount of processes to get even close enough to be successful, yet here we are. The hunter is drawing from a lifetime of human experiences, each executing within the mind, like a symphony, to simultaneously produce the desired results. All of this is being multitasked in the subconscious, with the hunter possibly never even thinking a single conscious word, besides their version of 'hungry'. This is true human multitasking and it is a beautiful thing.

I have to remember that the brain is an analogue computer, totally different than a digital one. Few realize the beauty and power of analogue, thinking digital is better because it is the now and the future. The core difference between the two, in my mind, is that analog is tremendous in it's ability to store data, but also that the data itself is truly unlimited. Analog data has a depth and beauty that digital data simply can never encode, or recreate.

A very simple aspect of this, to illustrate my point, is that of analogue audio vs digital audio. Analogue audio essentially captures the actual waves created by our voice and converts the sound waves into electrical waves, with the highest degree of accuracy possible. In fact this accuracy is unlimited as I'll soon show you.

The problem with analogue audio is the amount of storage required to contain it, is enormously bulky and does not scale at all well, unlike digital data. When every digital recording starts it is an analogue stream of electrical data in the form of a wave. The digital recording chops this analogue data into little chunks defined by the frequency limits of the human ear. If we can't hear it, why bother encoding it? The sine wave of the audio itself is a pure unlimited stream of data, however we only have so much digital storage space, so during the encoding process the amount of data is also limited to the point at which the analogue audio sounds is maintained, but all the rest of the analogue data is completely discarded. So, why then does digital audio 'sound' clearer?

Because it is, but it's just an audio illusion. The quality at which consumer's analogue equipment was horrible, compared to new digital technology. Parts of the audio become clearer, as only what we can actually hear, are left. This allows our minds to greater isolate the individual sounds, eliminating hiss and artifacts from the original recording, but also the high peaks are removed, which is distorted in our ears and becomes just noise in our minds. But remember, all of this lost data would have been present during the original live production of the audio. Note however, an old cassette tape more accurately represents the audio than a CD does. This is also why all professional recording studios as based on analogue recordings. You can't have a digital recording without it first being analogue sound data, the absolute pristine version of data.

Ok, here's an example of the power of analogue data. In my very early career, I worked for the premier company to compress data, STAC Electronics. Our product was Stacker disk compression software. One idea proposed, by who I've no idea is the most beautiful and impossible for of data compression.

Imagine all the data Google has in every one of their data warehouses. It's all just a very long stream of 0's and 1's. So imagine we put a decimal point to start that enormous list of 0's and 1's. We would end up with a fraction, such as this:
.00011101010110101010100010111100110101010100010101001010101010101001010......n(google data)

Now imagine a piece of metal EXACTLY 1 meter long, or even 1 nanometer long. Does not matter. If humans had the mechanical capacity to cut that piece of metal into the exact fraction represented by all the Google data, it would be completely encoded and will never decay, as magnetic storage currently does. It is the most perfect way I know of, to encode enormous amounts of data into the smallest possible storage device. Obviously, the technology for such an encoding is way beyond humanity and does reach a limit at which atoms themselves can not be split to represent a fraction, but this is such a beautiful concept, I wanted to share it. Even an irrational number such as Pi can best be encoded with the fraction of 355/113. The point is that fractions are a form of analogue data. Digital data struggles to represent any fraction, with entire numeric types created to handle things like money, which even at their best, will never perfectly represent simply monetary exchanges involving fractions, or change. Forget about interest.

I want to wonder what our minds were like before we had words to capture thoughts themselves. I can envision the very easy process we went through creating words. A mother screams at a child "Nar!" when they reach out to touch fire, and the child learns immediately what Nar means, at the most simple concept of danger or stop or 'mom is going to hit me' so possibly even run. A simple word is created in a tight human family group, and that word will evolve through the use by the children, probably not the mother, who will learn the children's different interpretation of Nar. Possibly Nara may become fire, Narba is the unknown darkness for their world, and Naro is death. Simple words, used to convey the most essential ideas required for survival.

Obviously the strength of the family unit and it's growth determines the spread of their words. Interaction with other family units allow the vocabulary to grow. I'd imagine what brings a word into existence is consistency. A prehistoric mother that screams a different word of warning to their child will never properly communicate. I've no doubt this became very clear to our early minds simply by watching nature and the limited vocabulary and range of sounds that animals make. I would even go as far as to say early humans probably mimicked animal sounds as we developed our own words. Could it then be said that animals taught us how to speak? Who knows?

My question though, is what were our minds like before we had words, before we associated sounds with meaning. This was mostly likely a very short time in our mind's development, as pointed out above, but there was certainly a period when a group of humans had no words themselves.

So, for the hour or so (whatever), this condition existed in the mind, what was it like. Was it like a perpetual state of meditation, with no interrupting thoughts to interrupt the constant stream of emotions, feelings, and inspiration the subconscious mind produces? Although an absolutely beautiful existence, as perceived in my cozy apartment, a terrifying existence in the unforgiving wild of prehistoric life. I would give a year of my life, if I could only experience this now, for a single day.

It really makes me wonder the changed perception I'd have of our most difficult concept, love. Without all the words to go along with modern love, what would it be like? What would it feel like, to be held by a parent without any thoughts at all, or to look into their eyes with no words to distract from the pure emotion dominating my quiet mind?

Disney writes a lot about True Love. Hmmm, I would argue Disney doesn't know shit about love. I would think that art is one of the few things left in our reality that can evoke the flora of emotions at the level prehistoric people must have experienced. But even currently looking a the works of Leonardo, I find this almost impossible for my mind to accomplish.

I have struggled terribly as of late, having starting years ago when I went into recovery from drugs, with the concept of love. I took this to my sponsor at the time and was told "There is a difference between the love inside recovery rooms, and outside the rooms." Unfortunately, I did not live by that lesson and my current believe of love is in tatters, especially considering my own actions as of late. It is a really terrible thing to realize you terribly guilty of the crime that you were accusing others of committing.

I just remembered the topic of what I wanted to write about, but the realization I wanted to capture is long gone. The topic was Giacomo Caprotti, the young lover of Leonardo in 1490 nicknamed Salai or "little demon". He was only 10 when he first lived in Leonardo house, and I'll not reflect on that relationship, besides saying I believe Leonardo was a honorable person, however Salai was quite possibly the first Brat ever. Considering the age different, later in life, that relationship must have been fire at all times. Leonardo wrote more about his life companion Salai, than anything else, so I should read that before I go any further on this topic.

Nope, writing that did not spur the realization back into though. Sigh. Silly subconsciousness. I'd smoke a cigarette if I had one, and if it wasn't freezing outside.

item.title: Disposable Vape Poison
item.dc:creator: mmichaelis0812
item.content:encoded:
12/12/2024
TL;DR Dispose of lithium properly, childhood poisoning, and I flush 'DO NOT FLUSH' 'wipes.

I am very disappointed, but not surprised by the domination of disposable vapes in our society. I personally vape with a refillable pod vape. I'm also the type that actually collects (most) used alkaline and lithium batteries in my life, later disposing of them at Best Buy, where they will properly recycle them.

Everybody should know how toxic and dangerous lithium is. If they don't they are either too young to vape, or they have cognitive limitations. When a lithium battery is no longer in good condition, that does not mean all the lithium is gone. It's all still there, just like when it was brand new.

In a current global climate existential crisis as again, all but the young should be aware of, and knowing full well the cause of this crisis is human's inability to stop polluting our environment with toxic wastes, you would think that the young generation of our society would place considerable value on changing, at least their own ways. I've no doubt that they do want this change in their world, only the ignorant young, and mentally incompetent would not. Well, that's not true at all. There are plenty of intelligent adult people that completely disregard our future, out of greed. Ok, so I'm not talking to Trump, I'm talking to the respectable younger generations of this country.

Please think for a moment what happens to that toxic lithium once disposed of in common trash. The vape will most likely crack open due to the enormous pressures placed on it during processing and end up in a landfill somewhere. What is under ground that we all depend on for life? Our fresh drinking water, of course. And then we have rain from above which seeps into the cracked case, eroding whatever the lithium is encased in, eventually allowing it to seep into the soil and be carried great distance by running water.

How can generations of humans continue to disregard truths that they hold so dear and continue to pollute the Earth in this way? The answer has to lie in the society in which they exist. This is not the younger generation's problem, it's society's problem. The young are simply following in the footsteps of their predecessors, possibly taking a different step here or there, but ultimately walking the exact same path.

This is so obvious to me when I ponder disposable vapes. The marketing and the engineering goal of only connivence are probably two huge factors that still drive young consumers to opt for poisoning the earth, vs a little inconvenience of filling a pod infrequently.

I'm really at a loss of reasons a person would intentionally poison their environment, with the knowledge humans now possess. Does consumer convenience really trump rational logic so easily? Marketing will obviously drive the convenience message home, as well as all of it's other filthy magic. I just realized how guilty I am of the same fault, and I'm doing it on purpose.

After the election of Trump, again, I threw my hands up in the air and mostly thought 'whatever'. It was my counter to laying in bed in a futile attempt to understand my world anymore. It became whatever and I did my best to stop thinking. My heart did however desire something I could do to show my despair, in a way giving the middle finger to American society for their newly found open hatred of trans people like myself. It didn't take me long to find it, and I'll probably do it Trump's entire term.

I can not believe I'm going to say this, lol, whatever. When I use the restroom I use baby wipes (heated even). Toilet paper is so 1989, and having been many times to Thailand and Japan, I have experienced perfection in bathroom activities. During the covid toilet paper shortage, I hooked a sink sprayer to the water line of my toilet ($25 Menards) just like every toilet in Thailand has. Yes, it was very cold, but there is NOTHING that will wake you up better than spraying your butthole with freezing cold water!

Anyway, I'm avoiding telling my shame. Yes, I now flush even the wipes that say "DO NOT FLUSH". I rationalized that this does not cause Earth pollution, and any chemicals they contain are certainly less than that used by my kitchen dishwasher. So what does flushing it cause? It causes the sewer treatment plant to have to processes these items out of the sewage, at great expense. The only real harm is the operating cost of the treatment plant, which is passed on to consumers. I'm fine and happy to pay that cost, and well, considering America's current attitude toward a trans bitch like me, fuck everybody else. You really think I care what your sewage bill is every month? Fuck you America, lol!

So to wrap this up, I'm pretty much asking myself, why I even care about the Earth anymore if the majority of America doesn't give a flying fuck? What? 52% of Americans that voted care not at all about climate change. Why should I care? We recently hit an enormously terrible marker in science that means we are beyond the point of avoiding significant disaster. Nobody cares. Yes, I know plenty of people do care, I'm speaking in general terms, forgive me. At the time we passed that point of no return, more than half of us are not even willing to attempt to change, in fact 52% of voting Americans are thrilled that we will soon reverse course, abandon the world in their attempts to change, and instead produce more fossil fuels, the absolute poison of our existence. The purpose I guess for these changes, make some (white) people more money, and you know, save Kevin .18/g when filling up his piece of crap 1992 truck.

Ok, total change of subject, that was getting old anyway. My apartment neighbor acquired a 70's chevy van. I love it! However, he parks it outside my window facing front, so the exhaust is away from my window, but he runs it while he's working on it. The smell gets so terrible in my bedroom I have to leave and close the door. You know, the deadliest of exhaust fumes is carbon monoxide, which is totally invisible to humans. It is so damaging, because it has a affinity toward hemoglobin than oxygen alone. So once the blood is saturated with CO, even if actively breathing, the body receives no oxygen for a considerable period of time.

So thinking about this one day, I remembered my childhood in the back of mom's old station wagon, not the back seat, the trunk area where we played. This was way before safety harness, or common sense things like that. Hell, we put lead in gasoline in those days with the sole purpose to make some white guy that owned the additive company billions of dollars. Engine valves did not require lead additives to function properly back then. It was a total scam.

But, what do I know, right? I mean I grew up in the back of a car, where the exhaust fumes collected at every traffic stop. It gives me a headache, literally, to think about it. As a teen my stepfather had an old Buick Rivera, piece of shit thing, but there was more room for myself and my brothers. We took it across country one time. That's when my parents discovered that the majority of places outside rural Missouri, no longer sell leaded gasoline. We actually went to auto stores to buy lead gas poison for us all to breath on our journey. Good times.
